match.reason: The bank point is a Year 11 NSW card that also covers combustion and its questions test combustion, so it is broader and deeper than the Year 10 synthesis and decomposition point and cannot be reused or adapted.

draft.title: Synthesis and decomposition
card: Two or more simple substances join to make one more complex substance. Magnesium and oxygen join to form magnesium oxide.
One compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. Water can be split into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity.
A synthesis reaction has one product. A decomposition reaction has one reactant. Count the reactants and products to tell them apart.
Decomposition needs energy to be supplied, such as heat, light or electricity. Copper carbonate heated strongly breaks into copper oxide and carbon dioxide.
draft.remember: Synthesis builds one product from simpler reactants. Decomposition breaks one reactant into simpler products.

a.q: Sodium and chlorine react to form sodium chloride. What type of reaction is this?
opts: Synthesis
Decomposition
Neutralisation
Displacement
a.why: Two simple substances join to make one compound, so it is synthesis. It is not decomposition, because nothing breaks down into simpler substances.
a.clue: Count how many substances react and how many form.

b.q: Hydrogen peroxide in a bottle slowly forms water and oxygen gas. Which statement describes this reaction?
opts: Decomposition, because one compound forms simpler substances
Synthesis, because a gas is made as a new product
Synthesis, because two products form from the reaction
Decomposition, because oxygen is one of the products
b.why: One compound breaks into two simpler substances, so it is decomposition. Having two products does not make it synthesis. Synthesis has a single product made from simpler reactants.
b.clue: Look at how many reactants there are, not how many products.

b.best: Decomposition, because one compound forms simpler substances

problems.detail: The card says decomposition 'needs energy to be supplied, such as heat, light or electricity'. That is not true of every decomposition. Hydrogen peroxide decomposes on its own and releases energy. Question b's own example (a bottle slowly forming water and oxygen) contradicts the card. Use 'often needs' or 'many decompositions need' instead.

check.summary: The card says decomposition always needs energy supplied, which is false. Hydrogen peroxide, the example in question b, decomposes on its own and releases energy. Both questions are otherwise sound, with one clear answer each.

proposal.title: Synthesis and decomposition
card: Two or more simple substances join to make one more complex substance. Magnesium and oxygen join to form magnesium oxide.
One compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. Water can be split into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity.
A synthesis reaction has one product. A decomposition reaction has one reactant. Count the reactants and products to tell them apart.

Many decompositions need energy supplied, such as heat, light or electricity. Copper carbonate heated strongly breaks into copper oxide and carbon dioxide. Some compounds break down slowly on their own.
